title: WISE and 2MASS show no infrared excess from the light that TESS CPV dips block; blackbody dust below about 2,000 K that absorbs it is excluded for hosts and for young rapid rotators
abstract: We test if the material that makes complex periodic variable (CPV) dips re-emits the stellar light that it blocks. A clump with dip depth delta at x stellar radii intercepts at least delta/(4x^2) of the stellar luminosity. For 114 TESS hosts (median summed dip depth 0.147, x = 1.95), blackbody grains at the local equilibrium temperature (about 1,600 K) give a mean excess relative to W1 of +3.9% at W3, +1.1% at W2 and -2.2% at Ks. We compared AllWISE and 2MASS flux ratios of 21,488 colour-matched TESS M dwarfs, with corrections for colour, main-sequence height, age class and dip occultation. Young hosts minus matched non-hosts (78 vs 417) give W3 -0.85 +/- 0.67%, W2 +0.33 +/- 0.21% and Ks -0.23 +/- 0.41%. The amplitude relative to the prediction is A = 0.04 +/- 0.15 (A = 1 rejected at 6.3 sigma; 3.9 sigma with an equivalent-width estimator). Young minus old rapid rotators, each relative to slow rotators, give A = -0.20 +/- 0.19. Thus host-like blackbody dust around all young rapid rotators is also excluded. The mean absorbed fraction is below 0.0031 at 1,500 K and 0.0087 at 2,000 K (95%). No host has a strong W3 or W4 excess (0/106). Therefore the grains must scatter most of the light, stay hotter than about 2,000 K, or be fewer than the dips imply. Limitations: an estimator that uses only the deepest dip is not excluded for hosts (1.8 sigma), rapid rotators of all ages show a common 1% W2-W3 offset, and we did not compute grain optics.

display.caption: Infrared flux excess relative to W1 (observed minus dip occultation, 95% intervals) compared with the energy-budget predictions for blackbody grains. A: young CPV hosts minus matched non-hosts. B: old hosts minus non-hosts. C: young minus old rapid rotators, each relative to slow rotators. A is the fitted amplitude relative to each prediction.

95% upper limit on the mean absorbed fraction of stellar luminosity as a function of one common dust temperature (blue line; shaded region excluded), compared with the absorbed fraction that the dips require for three dip estimators (horizontal lines).

Flux excess relative to W1 of rapid (0.15-1 d) and moderate (1-2 d) rotators relative to stars without a period below 2 d, for young and old stars. The common offset of about 1% at W2 and W3 also occurs in old field stars and is therefore not from CPV material.
